topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture on the complement system and outlines its pedagogical context and perceived complexity.

topics.label: Complement System Overview, Nomenclature, and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture of the complement cascade, including its general biological roles, historical naming conventions, and the central function of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that converge to form C3 convertases and reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Activated Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream effector outcomes of complement activation: opsonization for phagocytosis, inflammatory mediation, and direct pathogen lysis via the membrane attack complex.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins that prevent bystander damage to host cells by controlling C3 convertase activity and membrane attack complex assembly.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the diverse clinical presentations, infection risks, and autoimmune phenotypes resulting from deficiencies in specific complement proteins and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Strategies Against Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular mechanisms pathogens develop to escape complement-mediated clearance, focusing on the strategies used by Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture Wrap-Up and Next Lecture Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and announces the upcoming lecture topic on the adaptive immune system.
